core_obligations: Parameterise the three classes: as in the cited book, the proof takes the three dominant weights representing the non-zero elements of the character group, the first being the highest weight of the natural representation, and records that its Tits algebra is trivial (proof lines 685-687).

The inner case: assuming the algebra is an inner form, which the author identifies with the square condition on the determinant, the proof reduces the criterion to the splitting behaviour of the even Clifford algebra over the quadratic extension generated by the discriminant (proof lines 687-708).

The outer case: for the outer forms the same computation over the imaginary quadratic extension L shows that the even Clifford algebra is central simple over L, and the author's equivalence then gives R-universality exactly when that algebra is split (proof lines 708-711).
Conclusion: the two alternatives of the statement (proof line 711).
proof_roadmap: 先按被引书 §27B type D_n 取代表 Z^* 三个非零元的支配权 λ、λ±，并记 D(λ) = Q 平凡。
内形式（即 (-1)^k det B 为平方）时把判据化到偶 Clifford 代数在判别式所生成的二次扩张上的分裂性；外形式时在虚二次扩张 L 上同样计算，由 RunivIff 得结论。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the R-universality criterion for the even special orthogonal algebra (author prop at source lines 673-682, label so2k), phrased through the even Clifford algebra and the sign or square condition on the determinant. The proof (source lines 684-712) computes the Tits algebras of the three character-group generators, identifies the relevant one with the even Clifford algebra over the quadratic extension, and then reads the two alternatives off the author's division-algebra description of R-universality; the inner and outer cases are separated by the square condition on the determinant (proof lines 687-711). The case distinction and the Clifford-algebra computation are the substance of the proof. H2.
